Pathogenic FOXP3 variants cause immune dysregulation polyendocrinopathy enteropathy X-linked (IPEX) syndrome, a progressive autoimmune disease resulting from disruption of the regulatory T cell (Treg) compartment. Assigning pathogenicity to novel variants in FOXP3 is challenging due to the heterogeneous phenotype and variable immunological abnormalities. The number of cells with demethylation at the Treg cell-specific demethylated region (TSDR) is an independent biomarker of IPEX. We aimed to investigate if diagnosing IPEX at presentation with isolated diabetes could allow for effective monitoring of disease progression and assess whether TSDR analysis can aid FOXP3 variant classification and predict disease course. We describe a large genetically diagnosed IPEX cohort ( n = 65) and 13 individuals with other monogenic autoimmunity subtypes in whom we quantified the proportion of cells with FOXP3 TSDR demethylation, normalized to the number with CD4 demethylation (%TSDR/CD4) and compare them to 29 unaffected controls. IPEX patients presenting with isolated diabetes (50/65, 77%) often later developed enteropathy (20/50, 40%) with a median interval of 23.5 weeks. %TSDR/CD4 was a good discriminator of IPEX vs. unaffected controls (ROC-AUC 0.81, median 13.6% vs. 8.5%, p < 0.0001) with higher levels of demethylation associated with more severe disease. Patients with other monogenic autoimmunity had a similar %TSDR/CD4 to controls (median 8.7%, p = 1.0). Identifying increased %TSDR/CD4 in patients with novel FOXP3 mutations presenting with isolated diabetes facilitates diagnosis and could offer an opportunity to monitor patients and begin immune modulatory treatment before onset of severe enteropathy. Diabetes UK 19/005971 issue-copyright-statement © Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2023 Introduction Immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked (IPEX) syndrome are caused by pathogenic variants in FOXP3 , a transcription factor critical for the development of functional regulatory T-cells (T regs ) [ 1 ]. IPEX patients usually present with rapidly progressing multiple autoimmunity, including autoimmune diabetes (typically neonatal diabetes; NDM; onset < 6 months), life-threatening enteropathy, and atopic dermatitis. It is this classic triad of symptoms that is often the catalyst for genetic testing. However, the clinical, immunological, and molecular phenotype is heterogeneous, and increasingly, patients are reported with atypical features or a milder clinical course [ 2 – 4 ]. For progressive or syndromic genetic disorders such as IPEX syndrome, an early and accurate genetic diagnosis can provide insight into prognosis and direct monitoring and treatment plans, often improving outcomes [ 5 ]. Gene panel testing has revolutionized genetic testing and highlighted the phenotypic variability associated with monogenic diseases such as IPEX syndrome, with pathogenic variants being reported in individuals without all the classic features of the genetic disorder [ 6 – 8 ]. In such cases, assigning pathogenicity to novel variants can be difficult and may rely on waiting for additional features to develop. Isolated NDM may be the first and only feature at testing for IPEX, which overlaps with > 30 other monogenic disorders including other “Tregopathies” (sometimes termed IPEX-like disorders) [ 3 , 9 , 10 ]. Variant interpretation is further complicated by a high proportion of maternally inherited variants making co-segregation analysis difficult and an alternatively spliced isoform of FOXP3 which makes variants in exon 2 challenging to interpret. Functional immune analyses can assist with understanding the impact of a FOXP3 variant. However, these techniques require fresh blood samples to be rapidly processed by specialist laboratories, which can be prohibitive due to cost, expertise needed, and remoteness of patients to the laboratory [ 10 , 11 ]. Quantitative assessment of immune cells by methylation-specific qPCR is an alternative option for the analysis of human leukocyte populations and can be used to quantify different cell types in whole-blood derived DNA [ 12 ]. This cost-effective method does not rely on fresh samples and can be easily performed in a genomics laboratory using existing samples taken for genetic testing. The T reg cell-specific demethylated region (Foxp3 TSDR) is an imprinted region within the FOXP3 locus that controls and stabilizes expression of FOXP3. De-methylation of the TSDR allows for stable FOXP3 expression and subsequent maintenance of T reg identity [ 13 ]. T reg count by flow cytometry is very tightly correlated with the number of cells with demethylation of the TSDR in healthy individuals but appears to be unphysiologically high in individuals with IPEX [ 14 ]. We report a large cohort of patients with IPEX syndrome ( n = 65) resulting from a hemizygous FOXP3 pathogenic variant identified by custom gene panel testing for monogenic NDM. We assessed whether genetically diagnosing IPEX at presentation with isolated NDM could offer a window in which to monitor and intervene before patients become critically ill. We then sought to assess if the number of cells characterized by a demethylated FOXP3 TSDR could have diagnostic and prognostic value in atypical IPEX. As described in the method section, we determined the number of blood cells with demethylated FOXP3 TSDR or a region in the CD4 locus specifically demethylated in T helper cells (demethylated CD4). These counts were initially analyzed relative to the number of all nucleated blood cells determined by the number of demethylated copies of a region of the GAPDH gene previously been shown to be demethylated in all cells (demethylated GAPDH). Based on these counts, we quantified the percentage of Tregs (% demethylated FOXP3 TSDR) and CD4 + T helper cells (% demethylated CD4) in leukocytes as well as the percentage of Tregs within the T helper cells (% demethylated FOXP3 TSDR/demethylated CD4 + , henceforth referred to as %TSDR/CD4).

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic and prognostic value of FOXP3 TSDR demethylation, specifically the %TSDR/CD4 ratio, for IPEX syndrome. It found that increased %TSDR/CD4 serves as a robust discriminator for IPEX, particularly in patients presenting with isolated or neonatal diabetes and pathogenic FOXP3 variants. The biomarker is associated with more severe disease and aids in variant classification, early diagnosis, monitoring, and potential intervention before severe enteropathy develops.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic and prognostic biomarker analysis for IPEX syndrome using epigenetic methods
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study quantified the ratio of FOXP3 TSDR demethylation to CD4 demethylation (%TSDR/CD4) in whole-blood derived DNA using methylation-specific qPCR. This involved targeting demethylated CpGs in FOXP3 TSDR and CD4 loci. The median %TSDR/CD4 was 13.6% in IPEX patients versus 8.5% in unaffected controls (p < 0.0001), and 8.7% in other monogenic autoimmunity. An optimal diagnostic cut-off of 13.4% for %TSDR/CD4 was identified. Higher levels of demethylation were associated with more severe disease. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported as the focus was on diagnostic utility.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Calculated ratio of DNA methylation status (FOXP3 TSDR to CD4) via epigenetic qPCR

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median 13.6% [IQR 10.5–22.3] in IPEX patients (n=41) compared to male controls (n=29; median 8.5% [IQR 7.7–10.4], P < 0.0001). In other monogenic autoimmunity, median was 8.7% [IQR 7.4–12.7] (P = 0.01 vs IPEX). An optimal diagnostic cut-off of 13.4% was identified (51% sensitivity, ROC-AUC 0.81). Higher levels are associated with more severe disease (89% of patients with values ≥ 13.4% had ≥ 2 affected systems vs. 44% for those < 13.4%, P = 0.009). Values were observed to increase gradually from normal newborn blood spot values during disease progression.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the relative proportion of regulatory T cells (Tregs) within the CD4+ T cell population. It is a specific marker of thymic-derived Tregs, controlling and stabilizing FOXP3 expression critical for Treg identity and function. An elevated ratio indicates an imbalance in immune regulation associated with FOXP3-related immunodysregulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Early and rapid diagnosis of IPEX syndrome, particularly in patients presenting with isolated or neonatal diabetes and FOXP3 variants (including novel variants of uncertain significance). It is also used for monitoring disease progression and assessing disease severity (e.g., in cases of enteropathy or other monogenic autoimmunity features).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as an independent, useful, and specific diagnostic biomarker for IPEX syndrome, distinguishing it from other Treg insufficiencies. It facilitates early and accurate diagnosis, aids in the classification of FOXP3 variants, and is a good discriminator between IPEX and unaffected controls (ROC-AUC 0.81). Higher levels indicate more severe disease, predict disease course, and are associated with increased IPEX severity (values ≥ 13.4% correlate with ≥ 2 affected systems), offering an opportunity for early intervention to prevent severe complications like enteropathy.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript (demethylation status via epigenetic qPCR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased as a percentage of demethylated GAPDH from whole blood compared to healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Demethylation of the FOXP3 TSDR region is characteristic of stably committed regulatory T cells (Tregs) and is essential for their suppressive function and lineage stability. FOXP3 is a master regulator of Treg development and function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: IPEX patients with genetically confirmed FOXP3 variants (median disease duration 11.2 weeks) compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the percentage of Treg cells and, when elevated, suggests dysregulation associated with IPEX syndrome, aiding in rapid diagnosis.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript (demethylation status via epigenetic qPCR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Slightly reduced demethylation as a percentage of demethylated GAPDH from whole blood compared to healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Demethylation of the CD4 locus is characteristic of CD4+ T helper cells. CD4 is a glycoprotein expressed on T helper cells, essential for immune response. Its demethylation status indicates the proportion of CD4+ T cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: IPEX patients with genetically confirmed FOXP3 variants (median disease duration 11.2 weeks) compared to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Used in combination with % demethylated FOXP3 TSDR to calculate the %TSDR/CD4 ratio, which is critical for diagnosing IPEX.
